jobs.prompt:
Split the requirements of stage S10 (Swarm Watch Command Center (Hive overview, project cockpit, command palette, tools hub)) of "Project Swarm roadmap (audit 2026-10-20)" into small build tickets.
Return ONE JSON file named by the job output: a JSON array of ticket objects, nothing else.
Each ticket object has these fields:
key (short unique name in this file), title (under 140 characters), type (build, test, docs, migration, design, contract or human),
epic (a feature group name), scopeRefs (requirement ids, at least one for build, test, docs, migration), acceptance (1 to 5 observable checks; required for build, test, migration),
files (the files this ticket writes: repo-relative paths WITH their folders, for example src/app/page.tsx or supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql, never a bare file name unless the file really lives at the repo root; the scope header may allow additional exact root names with `Root files: a.json, b.txt`; never a folder, never an absolute path, never a dot-env file: use env.example.txt for an env template), deletes (existing files this ticket must delete, each named exactly; omit when none), dependencies (new npm packages the ticket needs, like zod or zod@^3.23.0; the runner installs them and the change goes through the security gate; omit when none), context (files it reads), contracts (contract files it uses), tests (the test files that prove this ticket: a build ticket lists the test files owned by its test ticket and depends on that test ticket; a test ticket lists its own), screens (only on UI tickets: the ids of the design screens the ticket renders, from the profile ui screens), dependsOn (keys of other tickets in this file, or ids of existing open tickets when listed below),
size (S or M; never larger: split instead), risk (low, medium or high), sensitive (true for payments, auth or customer data), steps (only for human tickets: 1 to 30 short imperative steps), skeleton (true only on the tickets of the thinnest vertical slice of the first stage: database, API, screen and test, the smallest path through the product; omit it elsewhere).
Rules: no ticket may gate more than 8 others: shared work (shared CSS, layout, i18n keys, types) is split early into one small ticket per component or file group, so one blocked ticket cannot hold half a stage; every requirement is covered by at least one ticket; every ticket traces to a requirement; two open tickets that can run at the same time never write the same file unless one depends on the other (dependsOn);
put shared types or contracts first and make the tickets that use them depend on them; add a test ticket for each requirement group.
Every build, test and migration ticket has at least one acceptance line (copy the requirement's own acceptance line when you have nothing more exact). A test never runs before the module it imports exists: prefer listing a module's test files in that build ticket's "tests" field over a separate test ticket, and when a separate test ticket is needed it is written to run after the build tickets it tests (the runner orders it after them).
A ticket of type contract writes exactly one OpenAPI 3 JSON file under contracts/ (for example contracts/api.json) using only paths (get, post, put, patch, delete, each with an operationId), components.schemas and local $ref; TypeScript, SQL and YAML types belong in build tickets that depend on the contract ticket.
Migration tickets write DDL only; their tests are separate tickets in a tests folder.
Keep every ticket small enough for one worker answer: at most 4 files, each file under about 12 KB when written; split a bigger feature into several tickets (the output of one worker is capped at about 15 KB per file).
Tools: when an acceptance check or test runs a tool command (supabase, cypress, prisma, drizzle-kit), a ticket must write that tool's config file (for example supabase/config.toml, cypress.config.ts) unless the project already has it.
Wiring rule: for every requirement that has build tickets, add ONE integration ticket (type build, "integration": true) that mounts those modules in the real routes, pages or entry points (for example src/app/.../page.tsx, a router file, an API route file) so a user can reach the feature.
Its "tests" lists a route-level or end-to-end test that requests the real route or page and checks the result (not a unit test of one module); its acceptance names the route or page; its scopeRefs are the requirement ids; its files are the route and page files only.
You do not need to list its dependsOn on the module tickets of the same requirement: the runner adds them. Two integration tickets that edit the same shared file (router, navigation, layout) are chained by the runner, the later one after the earlier.
A requirement is done only when its integration ticket is done and its route-level test passed.
Root rules (follow exactly in addition to the rules above):
1. Never put a file in a ticket's context or reads unless it exists in the repo now or is produced by a ticket in its dependsOn chain (the producer must be an ancestor).
2. Two tickets in the same wave never write the same file: chain them with dependsOn or merge them.
3. A test ticket is never in a later stage or wave than the code it tests: put tests in the build ticket's own outputs, or a test ticket that dependsOn it in the same stage.
4. Protected files (coordination/checks.json, .project-swarm.json, .swarm/, .git/ and the project's protected paths) are never assigned to worker tickets: route them to an owner-window human ticket.
5. Every requirement with build tickets gets exactly one integration ticket that mounts the modules in the real entry point (route, CLI command or page) with a route-level or end-to-end test.
Write ONLY integration tickets (every ticket has "integration": true). The module tickets below already exist; do not repeat them.
Existing module tickets of R-074: T-0347 Shared lane colour tokens and state mapping for agent robot heads (tools/watch-assets/robot-tokens.js); T-0348 Robot head component per lane and state for every agent avatar (tools/watch-assets/robot-head.js); T-0349 Kenney emote bubbles and Fluent animated badges layered on robot heads (tools/watch-assets/robot-emote.js)

R-074: Real robot heads are used everywhere an agent appears.
  - UI mounts `tools/watch-assets/robot-*.js` for every agent avatar; lane colours and states (working, thinking, sleeping, error, idle) match the All Projects page mapping.
  - Kenney emote bubbles and Fluent animated badges layer on robot heads; no stand-in SVG silhouettes ship in production bundles.
  - A snapshot test compares lane colour tokens on Command Center robot heads to the All Projects baseline file.
R-075: Signature glitch style uses PowerGlitch within strict limits.
  - Glitch-in on first load and on Hive→Cockpit switches; brain flickers on event bursts; hover glitch on project names, ticket ids, and robot heads; CountUp updates get a brief glitch; needs-you chips glitch once then stay still; failures and rate limits use stronger red or amber glitch; section headings glitch reveal on scroll into view.
  - Each burst lasts under 400 ms, never loops continuously, never runs on text actively updating, and at most 3 glitches run at once; all effects disable when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set.
  - `npm test -- tests/command-center-glitch-limits.test.mjs` exits 0 and asserts burst duration, concurrency cap, and reduced-motion off state.
R-076: A command palette jumps to projects, tickets, runs, PRs, docs, and commands.
  - Cmd-K on macOS and Ctrl-K elsewhere opens the palette with fuzzy search across projects, tickets, runs, PRs, docs, and swarm commands.
  - Arrow keys move selection and Enter navigates; recent items appear at the top after use.
  - Choosing a project opens Project Cockpit; choosing a doc opens the Resources hub entry.
R-077: A first-visit guided tour explains the Command Center.
  - On first visit a skippable tour highlights the Hive, Project Cockpit, colour legend, and command palette in plain language.
  - Help menu includes Replay tour, which restarts the tour without clearing completion for other users.
  - Tour steps are reachable by keyboard and dismiss with Escape.
R-079: The phone layout stacks the Hive and tabs the Cockpit without horizontal scroll.
  - At 390 px width the Hive layout is a vertical stack with no horizontal scroll in Playwright.
  - Project Cockpit uses tabs for orchestrator, tickets, and run stream at phone width.
  - Interactive targets measure at least 44 px in both dimensions on phone layout tests.
